name: r3c1 + 3 epochs (more samples)
hypothesis: r3c1's network and 128 worlds, with 3 PPO epochs instead of 4. The budget then gives about 1.3x more samples (about 159k steps) and about 78 updates instead of 58. r3c1's training success leveled off near 0.85 late in training, so more fresh data may help more than a fourth pass over old data. Refuted if dev success falls below 0.83.
last_analysis: Two things matter most. First, the policy head must pool over the flipped features (mirror-concat), so it scores the cells where a brick will really land. Second, the DONE head should see the detached placement logits. Halving n_envs to 128 (r3c1) lifted dev success from 0.68 to 0.88, with both seeds close together. r2c3 and r3c1 both took 3,712 gradient steps with 128-sample minibatches. So the gain came from collecting data with a more recent policy, not from more optimisation. The training curve for r3c1 levels off at about 0.85 from 75% of training onward. A footprint-shaped convolution in the head (r3c2) did worse. Gamma 0.99 (r3c3) also did worse. 2 epochs (r2c2) was mixed and noisy. For the last round, all three candidates keep the r3c1 network and push further along the axis that worked. One halves n_envs again to 64. One uses 3 epochs, which buys more samples and updates. One combines both changes to give the best chance at the final result.
